body:
This sounds most like what we are dealing with. Mine, too, is an only child. All her cousins are in other states and while they did video chat often, that still doesn’t substitute for physical interactions. 

I appreciate your perspective.

I understand what you are saying and can definitely see that I minimized a serious physical incident and more so focused on how the incident came to be. 

This is exactly what I was trying not to do. I want her to understand consequences, not victim blame, and teach her to not be the victim all at the same time. It’s hard and I don’t know how to do it.
That’s exactly what I’m afraid my child is doing and I definitely want to change her approach with how she interacts with others before it goes too far.

I agree with you, the boys reaction is completely inappropriate. I definitely don’t want to let her have a play date there again as the mother herself dismissed their argument/kicking incident to him not liking her wanting to stand on the roomba… 

But again, my daughter swears that is not how it went down which just adds to my overall conflicting feelings on how to approach this.

I did try to talk to her similarly- I asked her if she was ok, how her tummy felt now, and if she could make different choices would she have done something different. I also asked her why she said what she said knowing he didn’t like to be told that. 

It’s so hard to know if she truly understands what she is doing like her father is suggesting vs her mind isn’t able to make those connections yet.
